7.name: receives discharge order
7.description: Asha receives the discharge order and confirms Bridgepoint has a bed available for her father.
evidence: the discharge order landed in Asha's inbox and Bridgepoint's intake coordinator confirmed the bed at four-forty-one

7.name: watches father prepared for transport
7.description: After nearly six hours at her father's bedside, Asha watches the orderly verify his wristband and sees her father drift toward her without fully recognizing her.
evidence: Asha had been at her father's bedside for almost six hours
She watched the transport orderly check the wristband against the paperwork, watched her father's eyes drift toward her without quite finding her

7.name: feels aftermath of crisis
7.description: Asha experiences the emptiness that follows once the immediate crisis has finally been resolved.
evidence: felt the particular emptiness that came after a thing was actually done

7.name: receives urgent work messages
7.description: During the drive back to Philadelphia, Asha's phone fills with ignored messages from her firm and opposing counsel.
evidence: somewhere around the Delaware bridge her phone began stacking up the messages she had been ignoring since Tuesday—three from her paralegal, one from the managing partner marked urgent, and a forwarded complaint from opposing counsel on the Hatcher matter with a timestamp from that morning

7.name: conceals absence from firm
7.description: Asha reflects that she told her firm she needed personal time but did not disclose that she had effectively disappeared from a custody mediation and allowed filings to go out without her review.
evidence: She had told her firm she needed personal time.

She had not told them she had effectively vanished from a contested custody mediation she was lead on, that filings had gone out under her name without her review, or that a junior associate had signed something Tuesday afternoon that Asha herself would never have signed.

7.name: faces looming hearing deadline
7.description: Asha notes that the Hatcher hearing is scheduled for Monday morning, raising the stakes of her work crisis.
evidence: The Hatcher hearing was Monday at nine.

7.name: returns home and reviews complaint
7.description: After arriving on her block at night, Asha sits in her parked car and reads the complaint twice before going inside.
evidence: By the time she pulled into her own block the streetlights were on, and she sat in the parked car reading the complaint twice through before she let herself go inside.

7.name: enters apartment with work in hand
7.description: Inside her home, Asha leaves her coat behind and brings her laptop to the dining table to continue dealing with work.
evidence: Inside, Asha left her coat on the kitchen chair and carried the laptop to the dining table

7.name: reads complaint in parked car
7.description: Asha sits in a parked car and reads the complaint twice before going inside.
evidence: she sat in the parked car reading the complaint twice through before she let herself go inside

7.name: enters house and avoids couch
7.description: Inside, Asha leaves her coat on a kitchen chair and takes her laptop to the dining table instead of the couch, signaling her exhaustion.
evidence: Inside, Asha left her coat on the kitchen chair and carried the laptop to the dining table where she usually sorted mail, because sitting on the couch would have meant admitting how tired she was.

7.name: reads managing partner message
7.description: Asha opens the managing partner's message and reads it, then rereads it more slowly when she reaches the filing request.
evidence: She opened the managing partner's message first, read it once at the speed she read everything, then read it again more slowly when she got to the line naming the Tuesday filing by docket number and asking, in the controlled phrasing partners used when they were already drafting a record, for her to come in Sunday afternoon prepared to walk him through it.

7.name: finds filed motion with her signature
7.description: Asha checks the firm's document system and finds the Hatcher motion filed Tuesday with her name on it and a junior associate's certification stamp beneath it.
evidence: She pulled up the firm's document system in a second window and found the Hatcher motion filed Tuesday at 2:14 p.m., her name typed on the signature block and, beneath it, the small electronic certification stamp belonging to the junior associate she had been mentoring for two years.

7.name: cannot remember Tuesday afternoon
7.description: Asha stares at the filing timestamp and tries, unsuccessfully, to remember where she was at that moment because her father's condition had already worsened.
evidence: For a long minute she did not scroll; she only looked at the timestamp and tried to remember where she had been at 2:14 on Tuesday, and could not, because by then her father had already stopped recognizing the nurse and she had been on the phone with the social worker about a bed.

7.name: compares filing to draft
7.description: Asha opens the managing partner's message and her own draft folder side by side to compare the Tuesday filing with her unfinished Monday draft.
evidence: Asha opened the managing partner's message in full this time, then pulled up her own draft folder beside it and set the Tuesday filing alongside the version she had left half-finished on Monday night.

7.name: discovers troubling differences
7.description: Asha notices that the differences between the filing and her draft are small, which makes the discrepancy feel worse.
evidence: The differences were not large, which was worse;

7.name: compares draft versions
7.description: Asha lays out the Tuesday filing beside her unfinished Monday draft and notices the changes between them.
evidence: set the Tuesday filing alongside the version she had left half-finished on Monday night
The differences were not large, which was worse; whole paragraphs of her own language had been kept

7.name: realizes filing attribution risk
7.description: She understands that if she submits the filing as her own, no one will know it was altered, but if she objects the associate will be blamed in the record.
evidence: she walked into court Monday and read the filing as her own work, no one would ever know it had not been; if she said otherwise, the associate's name would be the one in the record

7.name: delays decision
7.description: Asha leaves both windows open and forces herself to reread the softened paragraph before deciding what to do.
evidence: She closed neither window
She sat with both of them open on the table, the kitchen quiet around her, and made herself read the softened paragraph a third time before she let herself decide anything

7.name: rewrites paragraph in own voice
7.description: Asha opens a blank document and starts retyping the softened paragraph in language she considers truly her own.
evidence: Asha opened a blank document beside the Tuesday filing and began retyping the softened paragraph in her own language
the way she would have written it Monday night if Monday night had belonged to her

7.name: tests revised motion for seams
7.description: She works carefully through the rewrite, checking whether it can be inserted into the motion without revealing the changes.
evidence: She worked slowly, testing each clause against the record, watching whether her version could be slid back into the motion without leaving the seams visible

7.name: considers using associate's certification
7.description: Asha wonders whether the associate's certification stamp can cover work that is now substantively hers again.
evidence: whether, in other words, the associate's certification stamp could be made to cover work that was now substantively hers again

7.name: receives phone notification
7.description: Before finishing the second sentence, Asha's phone lights up, interrupting her work.
evidence: She was halfway through the second sentence when her phone lit on

7.name: receives Rosa's text update
7.description: Asha's phone lights up with a message from Rosa saying the papers are notarized and she is heading home.
evidence: her phone lit on the table: Rosa, three lines, papers are notarized, heading home now.

7.name: sets phone aside and resumes writing
7.description: Asha reads the message, puts the phone face down, and returns to her writing with a brief sense of focus.
evidence: Asha read it, set the phone face down, and went back to the paragraph
for a moment the dining table felt smaller, the Trenton end of the week folded shut enough that she could keep her eyes on the screen.

7.name: leaves revision unfinished
7.description: Asha decides the revised sentence still does not fit but leaves it on the page and moves on.
evidence: The revised sentence still did not quite fit, and she left it on the page anyway and moved to the next one.

7.name: reviews transferred work items
7.description: Asha closes the draft and opens the paralegal's email to inspect the list of work that has been moved under her name since Tuesday.
evidence: Asha left the half-revised paragraph mid-sentence and closed the blank document, then opened the paralegal's email and began clicking through the list of everything that had moved under her name since Tuesday:

7.name: finds unfamiliar legal documents
7.description: She recognizes some items but discovers others she has never seen, including a discovery response and two letters to opposing counsel.
evidence: a continuance request she recognized, a discovery response she did not, two letters to opposing counsel she had never seen drafted.

7.name: realizes unfamiliar items exceed her grasp
7.description: Asha reads the dates and initials and feels the number of unfamiliar documents become too many to honestly treat as her own work.
evidence: She read down the column of dates and initials and felt the count of unfamiliar items grow past what she could plausibly absorb as her own without lying outright.

7.name: steps away for water
7.description: Overwhelmed, Asha pushes the laptop away, stands up, and goes to the counter for water.
evidence: After the fourth document she pushed the laptop a few inches away, stood, and walked to the counter for water;

7.name: stares at untouched water
7.description: Asha fills a glass but forgets to drink it, instead staring at the water as the kitchen light catches the rim.
evidence: she filled the glass and then forgot to drink it, looking instead at the level sitting still inside the glass while the kitchen light caught the rim.

7.name: delays returning to work
7.description: Back at the table, Asha lets the dimmed screen remain untouched for a moment before forcing herself to continue.
evidence: When she came back to the table the screen had dimmed, and she let it stay dim a moment longer before she touched the trackpad and made herself

7.name: returns to reading at the table
7.description: Asha comes back to the table and forces herself to keep reading after briefly letting the screen stay dim.
evidence: When she came back to the table the screen had dimmed, and she let it stay dim a moment longer before she touched the trackpad and made herself keep reading.

7.name: reviews legal files for changes
7.description: Asha works through the paralegal's list, opening unfamiliar filings and reading them to identify who altered each draft.
evidence: Asha pulled the laptop back toward her and worked down the paralegal's list one file at a time, opening the discovery response she did not recognize, then the two letters to opposing counsel, then a stipulation she had no memory of authorizing.
She read for the shape of the changes rather than the substance, looking for whose hand had been on each draft

7.name: detects pattern of softened edits
7.description: By the third document, Asha realizes the associate has repeatedly preserved her structure while weakening her hard lines.
evidence: by the third document a pattern was already showing: the associate had kept her structure and softened her edges, the same small retreat in every place where Asha would have held a line.

7.name: receives Rosa's message
7.description: Asha's phone buzzes with a text from Rosa saying the papers are done and she is ten minutes away.
evidence: Her phone buzzed against the wood and she turned it over without lifting it from the table. Rosa: Papers are done. I am ten minutes away. Put the kettle on.

7.name: prepares kitchen for Rosa's arrival
7.description: Asha decides to make the kitchen look normal for Rosa and to keep working because the filings will not shrink in ten minutes.
evidence: Asha read it twice, set the phone back down face up this time, and went to fill the kettle before returning to the screen, because the kitchen would need to look like a kitchen when Rosa came through the door, and because the list of filings was not going to be shorter in ten minutes than it was now.

7.name: closes files and sets up for arrival
7.description: Asha closes the documents, marks her place, and moves the laptop aside before starting the kettle.
evidence: Asha closed the open files one by one, marked her place in the paralegal's list, and slid the laptop to the far end of the table before standing to fill the kettle.

7.name: hears Rosa enter
7.description: Just after setting the kettle on the burner, Asha hears Rosa unlock the door and come inside.
evidence: She had just set it on the burner when she heard Rosa's key in the lock, and then Rosa was through the door

7.name: Asha clears the table
7.description: Asha moves the laptop aside and clears space at the table before turning to make tea.
evidence: slid the laptop to the far end of the table before standing to fill the kettle

7.name: Rosa arrives with notarized papers
7.description: Rosa enters with a manila envelope of notarized papers and places it on the table.
evidence: she heard Rosa's key in the lock, and then Rosa was through the door with the manila envelope of notarized papers in her hand, setting it down on the table beside where the laptop had been

7.name: Rosa checks Asha's mood
7.description: Rosa notices the cleared table, the envelope, and Asha's expression, then asks if she is okay.
evidence: Rosa took in the cleared table, the dimmed screen at the edge of it, the kettle that had not yet begun to whistle, and then Asha's face. "You okay?" she asked

7.name: Asha gives a hesitant reassurance
7.description: Asha says she is okay, then repeats it after a pause without fully meeting Rosa's gaze.
evidence: Asha said yes, and then, after a beat in which she did not quite look at the envelope, said it again

7.name: Asha opens the envelope
7.description: Asha reaches for the notarized papers and opens the manila envelope while avoiding Rosa's eyes.
evidence: Asha reached across the table and slid the manila envelope toward herself, her eyes on the metal clasp rather than on Rosa, and worked it open with her thumbnail

7.name: Rosa comforts Asha silently
7.description: Rosa places a light but persistent hand on Asha's shoulder and waits instead of pressing her again.
evidence: Rosa watched the second yes settle, then stepped around the corner of the table and laid a hand on Asha's shoulder, light enough to be brushed off and heavy enough not to be. She did not ask again; she only kept her hand there and waited for Asha to lift her face

7.name: Asha acknowledges Rosa's concern
7.description: Asha eventually lifts her face, and the two women silently acknowledge that her repeated reassurance was not believable.
evidence: Asha lifted it eventually, and what passed between them was less an answer than an acknowledgment that the answer she had given twice was not one either of them was going to pretend to believe

7.name: Kettle begins to whistle
7.description: The kettle starts to come to a boil in the background as the tense exchange continues.
evidence: Behind them the kettle began, low, not yet a whistle

7.name: Asha gently removes Rosa's hand
7.description: Asha lifts Rosa's hand from her shoulder with a careful, restrained gesture rather than a rejection.
evidence: Asha lifted her hand and eased Rosa's off her shoulder, not quickly, the gesture closer to setting something down than pushing

7.name: Asha gently removes Rosa's hand
7.description: Asha eases Rosa's hand off her shoulder in a controlled, non-rejecting gesture.
evidence: Asha lifted her hand and eased Rosa's off her shoulder, not quickly, the gesture closer to setting something down than pushing it away.

7.name: Asha stops the kettle before it whistles
7.description: Asha goes to the stove and removes the kettle before it can whistle, interrupting the rising sound.
evidence: She stood, crossed to the stove, and lifted the kettle off the burner before the low sound could climb into a whistle

7.name: Asha prepares tea for both women
7.description: Asha takes two cups, pours tea for herself and Rosa, and the ordinary task steadies her.
evidence: then took two cups from the shelf above the counter and poured for both of them
The water went in steady, and she watched it rather than Rosa, the small ordinary motion of the pour seeming to give her back the use of her hands.

7.name: Asha sets Rosa's cup down first
7.description: Asha returns to the table and places Rosa's cup down before her own, beside the envelope.
evidence: When she carried the cups to the table she set Rosa's down first, then her own beside the manila envelope

7.name: Asha resumes reading the envelope papers
7.description: Asha sits back down and opens the envelope's contents, preparing to examine the documents.
evidence: and only then did she sit back down in front of the open clasp and the papers waiting inside it
Asha drew the top filing from the envelope and laid it flat

7.name: Asha scrutinizes the associate's work
7.description: Asha reads the associate's Tuesday work line by line, focusing on wording choices and hedged details rather than the signature.
evidence: She went line by line through the associate's Tuesday work, looking less at the signature block than at the choices stacked above it: a softened verb where Asha would have left the harder one, a concession phrased as cooperation, a footnote that hedged a date she would have stated cleanly.

7.name: Rosa silently observes Asha reading
7.description: Rosa sits across from Asha, holds her cup, and watches her read without interrupting.
evidence: Rosa sat down across from her without speaking, wrapped both hands around the cup, and watched Asha's eyes track across the page.

7.name: Asha marks the document with corrections
7.description: Asha makes margin marks on the filing, signaling her disapproval of the associate's choices.
evidence: the small pen mark Asha made in the margin, and the second one a paragraph later, were answer enough

7.name: Asha marks the filing
7.description: Asha makes pen marks in the margin of the filing, signaling she has found issues in the document.
evidence: the small pen mark Asha made in the margin, and the second one a paragraph later
Asha did not look up to tell her

7.name: Asha silently claims responsibility
7.description: Asha finishes reading and slides the filing back, internally accepting that the edits and errors now belong to her signature.
evidence: Asha read to the bottom of the page, then slid the filing back toward the center of the table without looking up at Rosa.
the associate's softened verb, the hedged footnote, the date that should have been clean—all of it now belonged to her signature whether she said so on Monday or not.

7.name: Rosa allows a working silence
7.description: Rosa remains quiet while Asha processes the filing, and Asha appreciates that the silence is practical rather than comforting.
evidence: Across the table Rosa lifted her cup and did not speak, and Asha was grateful for the way Rosa let the silence be a working silence rather than a kind one.

7.name: Asha reviews additional filings
7.description: Asha pulls more filings from the envelope and examines them one by one, finding the same pattern of softened language and cautious citation.
evidence: Asha drew the next filing from the envelope and laid it beside the first, then a third, working through them one at a time without comment.
The pattern she had marked once held across the others in smaller ways: a qualifier where none was needed, a date given as on or about, a citation pulled a half step shy of the holding.

7.name: Rosa asks about fixing the language
7.description: Rosa asks Asha whether she preserves the softer wording in the filings or corrects it.
evidence: Rosa watched her line them up on the table, then set her cup down and asked, quietly, do you take the softer verbs, or do you fix them.

7.name: Asha pauses before answering
7.description: Asha does not respond immediately, finishing her current paragraph and making another mark instead.
evidence: Asha did not answer at first; she finished the paragraph she was on and made another mark

7.name: Rosa poses a choice about editing
7.description: Rosa quietly asks Asha whether she takes the softer verbs or fixes them, forcing the underlying editorial choice into the open.
evidence: do you take the softer verbs, or do you fix them.
Rosa had named, in eight words, the choice Asha had been circling since she opened the clasp.

7.name: Asha silently acknowledges the question
7.description: Asha finishes her paragraph and marks it before looking up, acknowledging Rosa's question without answering it verbally.
evidence: Asha did not answer at first; she finished the paragraph she was on and made another mark
When she finally looked up, it was not to answer but to acknowledge that Rosa had asked it out loud.

7.name: Rosa nudges the folder toward Asha
7.description: Rosa slides the manila folder closer and keeps her fingertips on it, signaling Asha to proceed.
evidence: Rosa reached across and slid the manila folder a half inch closer to Asha, then rested two fingertips on the cover and left them there.

7.name: Asha begins hardening the language
7.description: Asha uncaps her pen and starts replacing softened or hedged wording with firmer language in the filing.
evidence: Asha looked at the hand, not at Rosa, and uncapped her pen.
She drew a line through the softened verb in the first filing and wrote the harder one above it in her own small upright hand

7.name: Asha revises the remaining papers
7.description: Asha continues through the stack, changing hedged phrases and uncertain wording page by page without speaking.
evidence: then turned the page and did the same to the hedged footnote, and then to the on or about, working through the fan of papers in the order she had laid them out.
She did not say I am taking them and she did not say I am fixing them; she made the corrections in ink that would be hers on Monday

7.name: Rosa watches Asha edit in silence
7.description: Rosa observes Asha's corrections and keeps her hand on the folder until Asha finishes the last page.
evidence: and Rosa watched her do it and kept her fingertips where they were until Asha reached the last page.

7.name: Asha finishes the folder and signals completion
7.description: Asha closes the folder, caps her pen, and gives Rosa a small nod that indicates she has completed the task she came to do.
evidence: Asha closed the last folder and capped her pen with a small click that carried in the quiet of the kitchen.
she had done what she came to the table to do.

7.name: Asha acknowledges the corrections
7.description: Asha looks up at Rosa, nods once, and silently signals that she has completed the corrections she came to make.
evidence: looked up at Rosa for the first time since she had started, the corrected pages stacked under her hand, and gave one short nod that meant she had done what she came to the table to do

7.name: Rosa asks if Asha feels better
7.description: Rosa quietly asks Asha whether she feels better now, probing the emotional effect of the completed corrections.
evidence: Rosa drew her fingertips back from the cover, leaned into her chair, and said, quietly, do you feel better now

7.name: Asha withholds an immediate answer
7.description: Asha pauses instead of answering Rosa, revealing that the real issue is not the corrections but the unresolved question of the Tuesday signature.
evidence: Asha didn't answer right away; she set the pen down beside the stack and looked at the place on the folder where Rosa's hand had been

because the honest answer was that the corrections were the easy part and Rosa knew it, and the harder one—what to say about the Tuesday signature, and to whom—was still sitting on the table between them in ink that would be hers on Monday

7.name: Rosa presses for the truth about Tuesday
7.description: Rosa leans in and directly asks who will be told the truth about Tuesday, making the hidden issue explicit.
evidence: "Who gets the truth about Tuesday?" she asked

7.name: Asha counters with a question about witnesses
7.description: Asha avoids answering Rosa's question and instead asks who else saw the documents, shifting the issue to possible witnesses.
evidence: Asha didn't look away this time; she drew the corrected stack back toward her own side of the table, set her palm flat on the top folder where Rosa's fingertips had been, and after a moment asked, "Who else saw these?"
It was not an answer to Rosa's question

7.name: Both recognize the questions are equivalent
7.description: Rosa accepts Asha's non-answer, and both women understand that the two questions are really the same dilemma from different angles.
evidence: Rosa let it stand as not-an-answer, because the two questions were the same question approached from opposite sides, and both of them knew that whatever Asha decided about the second would decide the first

7.name: Asha reveals the Tuesday filing
7.description: Asha pulls the Tuesday filing out from under the corrected pages and places it between them, exposing the document at the center of their conflict.
evidence: Asha slid the Tuesday filing out from under the corrected stack and laid it flat between them

7.name: Asha prepares to continue handling the filing
7.description: Asha uncaps the pen again, then sets it down and reaches for the next step, signaling she is about to act on the filing.
evidence: She uncapped the pen again, but this time she set it down and reached for the

7.name: Asha reveals the Tuesday filing
7.description: Asha pulls the Tuesday filing from beneath the corrected stack and places it between herself and Rosa.
evidence: Asha slid the Tuesday filing out from under the corrected stack and laid it flat between them.

7.name: Asha marks the signature date
7.description: Asha switches to Rosa's red marker and draws an X through the date in the signature block, visibly altering the page.
evidence: she set it down and reached for the red marker Rosa had left near the napkin holder, and she drew a single X across the date in the signature block, deliberate enough that the ink bled a little into the fiber of the paper

7.name: Asha returns the marked page
7.description: After marking the date, Asha slides the page back beneath the rest of the stack.
evidence: before she eased the page back beneath the others

7.name: Rosa silently watches Asha's action
7.description: Rosa watches Asha mark the page without intervening, holding back until the action is complete.
evidence: Rosa watched the X go down and did not move until it was finished

7.name: Rosa withdraws from the table
7.description: Rosa pulls her hand back, folds it into her lap, and responds with a measured statement.
evidence: then she drew her hand fully back from the table, folded it into her lap, and said, evenly, only we did.

7.name: Rosa answers Asha's implied question
7.description: Rosa's reply addresses the question Asha asked rather than the one Rosa had asked first, shifting the exchange's meaning.
evidence: because Rosa had answered the question Asha had asked instead of the one Rosa had asked first

7.name: Both recognize the marked page as an opening answer
7.description: Asha and Rosa understand that the marked page is the beginning of an answer to the other question, not its conclusion.
evidence: they both understood that the marked page underneath was the beginning of an answer to the other one, not the end of it
